name: Face taping (Frownies / sleep patches)
lead: Face taping is the practice of applying adhesive patches or tape to areas of expression lines, such as the forehead, the vertical lines between the eyebrows and the corners of the eyes and mouth, usually overnight, to hold the skin flat and discourage the underlying muscles from creasing it. The best-known product is Frownies, an American brand of paper patches with a water-activated adhesive [1].

Proponents say that holding the skin smooth and limiting muscle movement while it is worn can soften expression lines over weeks or months of consistent use. The manufacturer describes the effect as temporary and dependent on ongoing use [1]. No clinical trial of face-taping patches was found in the sources reviewed, and the claim that overnight taping reduces wrinkles has not been tested in published studies.
infobox: Unbleached Kraft paper with starch-based (dextrin) adhesive [1]
Forehead, between the brows, eye and mouth corners

paras: Frownies patches are made of weighted, unbleached Kraft paper coated with a hypoallergenic, vegetable-derived adhesive that activates when wetted and hardens, giving the patch a stiff, cast-like quality [1]. The manufacturer sells triangular patches for the forehead and between the eyes, and diamond and butterfly shapes for the corners of the eyes and mouth. A separate line, Gentle Lifts, uses smaller self-adhesive cotton-lined patches for fine areas such as lip lines [1].

The company describes the mechanism as mechanical rather than chemical: the patch acts as a splint that keeps the skin and muscle in a relaxed, flat position, with no active ingredient involved [1]. Some other products marketed as sleep patches or wrinkle tapes use silicone or medical-style tape to the same end.

According to the company's account, the product was invented in 1889 by Margaret Kroesen for her daughter Alice, a concert pianist and model who developed frown lines from furrowing her brow. It was originally sold as 'Wrinkle Eradicators' [1]. The business describes itself as family-owned and led by women across five generations, with fifth-generation leadership taking over in 2025 [1]. The brand reports renewed popularity through social media, including TikTok [1]. These historical details come from an AI-generated summary of company material and have not been independently verified.

The brand positions the patches as a non-invasive, drug-free alternative to injections such as botulinum toxin [1]. Medical references describe botulinum toxin as working by immobilizing the muscles that produce wrinkles, which is the same stated principle behind taping, though the two act through different means [2].

Wrinkles are attributed in medical sources to many factors, including sun damage, smoking, glycation, sleep position and repeated facial expression [2]. No published studies in the sources reviewed have measured whether taping changes wrinkle depth.

timeline.event: Margaret Kroesen creates adhesive patches later sold as 'Wrinkle Eradicators' / Frownies, per the company [1]
Fifth-generation leadership takes over the company [1]

card.summary: Paper or tape patches worn overnight to hold expression lines flat; a 130-year-old idea with no published trials.
card.aka: Frownies, wrinkle patches, sleep patches, forehead taping
card.note: Brand history is company-sourced; adhesive can irritate sensitive skin.

quick.overview:
Face taping means sticking patches over expression lines such as forehead and frown lines, typically overnight. Frownies, a brand dating to 1889 by its own account, is the best-known version.

Proponents say keeping the skin and muscles still softens lines over time. No published trial has tested this.
quick.mechanism: The patch is a stiff splint that holds skin flat and limits muscle creasing while worn. There is no active ingredient, and the maker says any effect is temporary.
quick.risks: No safety studies were found. As with any adhesive on the skin, irritation is possible; products are sold as cosmetics rather than medical devices.
